title: Nebula around star cluster RCW 38
caption: The region around the star cluster RCW 38, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: RCW 38 · constellation Vela · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This wide view from ESO's La Silla Observatory takes in the region around RCW 38, a star cluster about 5,500 light-years away in the direction of Vela, the Sails. It is what astronomers call an embedded cluster, meaning its stars are still wrapped in the cloud of gas and dust from which they formed.

Life there is harsh. Young, giant stars batter nearby fledgling suns and planets with powerful winds and floods of light, aided by massive stars that live fast and end as supernovae. At times this onslaught boils away material that might otherwise have gone on to build new planetary systems.

Scientists think our own Solar System emerged from a similarly violent setting, which makes regions like RCW 38 useful for understanding our own origins. An embedded cluster is a snapshot of star formation still under way, before the stars have cleared away the cloud they were born in.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.43 x 33.05 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 53 × 53 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope combines B, V, R and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, bringing out faint glowing gas around the cluster.
